newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria won't take control in privatised banks.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria won't take control in privatised banks.

text.p: Nigeria's military government is considering shelving the idea of taking golden shares in the privatised four biggest banks in the country, finance minister Anthony Ani said in an interview reported on Monday.
Ani told Thisday newspaper in an interview that a new banking decree was underway "to take care of government's intentions in the now rested golden share decree."
The idea of golden shares had been to enable government stop "unfit persons" from taking control of banks, he said, adding that this could now be achieved under the new banking decree.
The decree would disqualify anyone found guilty in the current clean-up of the banking sector or other financial offences from being a director of any bank.
Scores of bank executives have already been convicted by failed banks tribunals for fraud that shook the banking industry following the deregulation of the sector seven years ago.
Under the golden share option, the Nigerian government would have retained control over the biggest banks regardless of its shareholding.
But the private sector and the World Bank protested against this, arguing that it was against the spirit of privatisation.
The government divested from the country's four biggest banks; UBA, UBN, First Bank, Afribank, four years ago.
Collectively they hold huge government deposits and the authorities say they can not allow them to be distressed.
Ani said the government had no intention of re-acquiring shares in companies it had divested from.
"Government is only interested in ensuring that only fit and proper people become directors of privatised firms in the future," he said.
